expectations.text: Identifies the partial-failure / atomicity risk in /billing/cancel: stripe.subscriptions.cancel() is called before the DB update, so a DB failure after the Stripe call leaves state inconsistent with no rollback
expectations.evidence: CRITICAL-3: 'Cancel: Stripe Cancels but DB Update Can Fail — Divergence' — 'Stripe reports the subscription cancelled; if the DB update throws, the local record still shows active. The user cannot re-subscribe (Stripe rejects), UI shows active, and support has no automated path to detect it.'

expectations.text: Notes that the Stripe client is instantiated at module scope bypassing a secrets/config abstraction — it lacks an injection seam for testing and violates the adapter pattern
expectations.evidence: CRITICAL-1: 'this module-level singleton is untestable — tests cannot inject a mock client' and MEDIUM-1: 'Every handler directly imports db and instantiates stripe at module scope. There are no service interfaces, no repository abstractions, no dependency injection seams.' The fix also mentions: 'Inject the client via Fastify decorate or dependency injection so tests can substitute a mock.'

expectations.text: Identifies that the webhook handler embeds at least 3 distinct business event handlers (subscription updated, subscription deleted, invoice.payment_failed) inline rather than delegating to separate use cases or handlers
expectations.evidence: MEDIUM-4 code snippet shows: 'if (event.type === "customer.subscription.updated") { ... } if (event.type === "customer.subscription.deleted") { ... } if (event.type === "invoice.payment_failed") { ... }' and recommends: 'Use a structured switch/dispatch table instead of sequential if blocks for clarity and exhaustiveness.'

expectations.text: Recommends a StripeAdapter or StripePort (port/adapter pair) as the correct abstraction — not just 'inject the Stripe client'
expectations.evidence: The review recommends injecting the Stripe client via Fastify decorate or dependency injection and extracting a BillingService/BillingRepository, but never specifically recommends a StripeAdapter, StripePort, or a port/adapter pair as the correct abstraction. The Target Architecture shows 'StripeClient (external API adapter: injectable, mockable)' as a layer label but does not prescribe a StripeAdapter or StripePort interface pattern.

expectations.text: Notes that GET /billing/invoices has a write side effect (upsert into DB) making it non-idempotent and violating HTTP GET semantics — and that this decision logic belongs in a use case, not a route
expectations.evidence: HIGH-3: 'This GET handler writes to the database. This violates HTTP semantics (GET must be safe and idempotent).' Fix: 'Move the sync logic to an explicit POST /billing/invoices/sync or a background job triggered by webhooks.' The review also recommends extracting a BillingService (MEDIUM-1) so the decision logic moves out of the route, and P1 item 5 states 'Fix GET /billing/invoices to be read-only. Move sync logic out of the GET handler.'

needs_review: Expectation 4 (StripeAdapter/StripePort): The review mentions 'StripeClient (external API adapter: injectable, mockable)' in the Target Architecture diagram but does not use the term StripeAdapter or StripePort, and does not describe a formal port/adapter pair pattern. A lenient grader might give partial credit; strict grading marks this failed.
